# @iam2r/pi-upstream-compat

A [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) extension that fixes **two upstream
quirks Pi only handles for its own built-in providers** — both decided by model id,
so they work for any model served through a third-party gateway:

1. **OpenCode session affinity** — attach `x-opencode-session` / `x-opencode-client`
   to models whose id mentions `opencode`.
2. **Thinking-mode replay** — mark DeepSeek-family thinking models so Pi replays
   `reasoning_content` on assistant turns, which upstream requires.

## The problems

### 1. OpenCode session headers

Pi only sends OpenCode's session headers when the selected model is served by its
own built-in `opencode` / `opencode-go` providers, or when the request URL host is
exactly `opencode.ai`
([`getSessionHeaders()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-attribution.ts)).

Model ids also travel through third-party OpenAI-compatible gateways — for example
`builtin:opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` served by a custom provider. Pi sees the
gateway as the `provider`, so the gate can never match and **no session header is
sent at all**. Upstream then either

- rejects the request outright — `400 MissingSessionID` — or
- accepts it but derives a fresh session per request, destroying prompt-cache affinity
  (every turn pays full input-cache cost and latency).

### 2. Thinking-mode `reasoning_content`

DeepSeek-family thinking upstreams reject a replayed assistant turn that carries
`tool_calls` but no `reasoning_content`:

```
400 The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

Pi already knows how to satisfy that: a model with
`compat.requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` gets `reasoning_content: ""`
replayed on assistant messages. Pi sets that flag on its built-in `opencode-go` and
`deepseek` models, and its other detection is URL-based (`opencode.ai`,
`api.deepseek.com`) — never id-based. A model declared with a custom provider and a
gateway base URL therefore never gets the flag, and every tool-using turn fails.

## Install

```sh
pi install npm:@iam2r/pi-upstream-compat
```

For a single run without installing:

```sh
pi -e npm:@iam2r/pi-upstream-compat
```

Then restart Pi — extensions load at startup.

> **Renamed.** This package was published as `@iam2r/pi-opencode-session-header`
> up to 0.3.3. Replace it with the name above; the old `PI_OPENCODE_*` environment
> variables keep working, but `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_*` is the documented spelling now.

## What it matches

### Session headers

A request gets the session header when **any** of these hold:

| Condition                                           | Example                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| provider is `opencode` or `opencode-go`             | Pi's built-in providers                     |
| baseUrl host is exactly `opencode.ai`               | `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1`       |
| **model id contains `opencode`** (case-insensitive) | `builtin:opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` |

It appends `x-opencode-session` (the session id, see below) plus
`x-opencode-client: pi`, and never overwrites a header another layer already set.

The id rule is the one that breaks in practice, because a gateway need not keep the
upstream model name: `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, with no `opencode` anywhere in it,
matches nothing above. Set `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_MODEL_MATCH` to a comma-separated
list of extra substrings (for example `deepseek,v4.1`) and those ids are recognised
too.

### Thinking-mode compat

An assistant turn is replayed with `reasoning_content` when the **model id** contains
one of these fragments (case-insensitive):

| Default fragments                            | Family                                         |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `deepseek`, `kimi`, `glm`, `minimax`, `mimo` | thinking upstreams that require the field back |

Add more with `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_MATCH` (comma separated, **appended** to
the defaults — setting one extra family cannot silently switch DeepSeek off), and skip
individual ids with `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_EXCLUDE`.
`PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_NO_THINKING=1` disables this half of the extension entirely.

What the extension does for a matching model, right before Pi serializes the request:

- sets `model.reasoning = true` (unlocks Pi's thinking levels and is the gate Pi uses
  for the replay), unless the model already says `reasoning: true`
- sets `compat.requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages = true`, merging into an
  existing `compat` object and keeping its other flags
- leaves models that Pi's own catalog already defines untouched — for those, Pi's
  curated metadata is the better answer (and guessing over it by id would turn, say,
  a non-thinking `deepseek-chat` into a reasoning model)
- never mutates a frozen model: it hands the implementation a shallow copy instead

`reasoning: false` cannot express an opt-out: Pi's provider composer fills that default
for every `models.json` model that does not set it, so it is the normal state of the
gateway models this extension exists for. Use `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_EXCLUDE`
instead.

### Where it applies

1. **The session's model registry** (`session_start`, `model_select`,
   `before_agent_start`, header event) — capabilities the UI reads live on these
   objects (`AgentSession.supportsThinking()` checks `model.reasoning`), so decorating
   the registry is what makes thinking levels and the model picker agree with the
   request builder. Decoration is scoped to the provider in use and skips every model
   Pi's catalog defines.
2. **Before every request** in both layers below — guarantees the model the
   implementation actually receives is marked, including models a gateway adds after
   startup, and regardless of what the registry holds.

The decision is per request, so it also covers models added to `models.json` after Pi
started, and models whose ids a gateway rewrites.

> `pi --list-models` prints the catalog **without a session**, so its `thinking`
> column still says `no` for gateway models: no `session_start` fires there, and Pi
> exposes no model-registry handle at extension-load time. Inside a session the model
> is marked before the first turn.

> Marking a model as reasoning is not free — Pi offers thinking levels for it and may
> send reasoning parameters. The defaults stay narrow on purpose. If you add a family
> that is not actually a thinking model, expect upstream errors; drop it from
> `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_MATCH` or list the offending ids in
> `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_EXCLUDE`.

## Two layers

Neither mechanism covers every request path on its own, so both are installed.

1. **`before_provider_headers`** — the official event. Emitted only from the
   coding-agent SDK's request-options builder, which covers the main agent loop but
   **not** callers that invoke `ctx.modelRegistry.streamSimple(...)` directly.
   Extensions do that for side requests (pi-subagents' pruned-fork summaries, for
   example), and those would reach the gateway with no session header.

2. **An api-level wrapper** — `registerApiProvider()` around the api implementation
   named by `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_API` (default `openai-completions`). It injects for
   matching models, applies thinking compat, and delegates to the implementation it
   captured, so it sits **below** every caller and needs no knowledge of which
   provider serves the model.

Both layers are idempotent with each other: whichever sees the request first sets the
headers or model flag, and the second one finds nothing left to do.

The registry decoration above is idempotent too — repeated `session_start`s and model
switches only count models that still lack the flag.

### Why layer 2 is re-asserted on every session

Two host behaviours shape this layer.

First, it cannot be a named provider registration:

```js
// pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/loader.js
registerProvider: (name, config, extensionPath) => {
	runtime.pendingProviderRegistrations.push({ name, config, extensionPath });
};
```

The host drains `pendingProviderRegistrations` once, at extension-load time
(`extensions/runner.js:bindCore()`). A `pi.registerProvider(...)` call made _after_
that — from a `session_start` handler, say — only appends to a queue nobody reads
again, so it is silently dropped, even though the call returns normally. Wrapping the
api implementation sidesteps that queue, needs no provider id, and covers every
provider serving that api at once.

Second, Pi clears api overrides when a session reloads: `AgentSession.reload()`
(`core/agent-session.js`), which serves `/reload` and session replacement, calls
`resetApiProviders()` — every registration is dropped and only the built-ins are put
back. So the wrapper is installed while the factory runs **and** re-asserted on every
`session_start`. Re-installing is idempotent: the previous entry is dropped first, and
the wrapper delegates to a captured base instead of to the registry, so installs
cannot stack.

### Why the session id is read lazily

The api wrapper runs outside any event context, so it needs a session id of its own.
The cache is filled on `session_start` and refreshed on every `before_provider_headers`,
and requests read the live session whenever that cache is empty — the session file
name (`<timestamp>_<id>.jsonl`) is the last resort. A context captured before a reload
counts as no answer instead of throwing.

This is hardening rather than a fix for a reproduced failure: at this extension's
`session_start` the id is already available (measured), so the cache is normally
populated before anything can ask. The fallback matters when it is not — an earlier
handler that yields for a while delays every handler after it, since Pi awaits them in
load order, and a session can be asked for a request while it starts.

The remaining boundary is inherent: a side request that arrives before any handler of
this extension has run cannot be helped. The request carries no session information of
its own, and Pi exposes no session id outside an event context (`ExtensionAPI` has no
session getter). Requests after the first handler are covered.

## Configuration

All optional, via environment variables. The pre-rename `PI_OPENCODE_*` names are
still read as fallbacks.

| Variable                              | Default              | Meaning                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_API`              | `openai-completions` | Api id(s) layer 2 wraps, comma separated. Every provider serving a model with one of these api ids is covered. |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_SESSION_STYLE`    | `raw`                | `raw` forwards Pi's session id verbatim. `canonical` derives a `ses_…` id instead.                             |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_MODEL_MATCH`      | _(unset)_            | Extra model-id substrings (comma separated) that also count as OpenCode, for gateways that rename them.        |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_NO_PROVIDER`      | _(unset)_            | Set to `1` to disable layer 2 and use the event hook alone.                                                    |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_MATCH`   | _(unset)_            | Extra model-id fragments that get the thinking-mode compat flag, appended to the defaults.                     |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_EXCLUDE` | _(unset)_            | Model-id fragments that keep their metadata as-is, e.g. a non-thinking model whose id mentions `deepseek`.     |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_NO_THINKING`      | _(unset)_            | Set to `1` to leave model metadata untouched.                                                                  |
| `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_DEBUG`            | _(unset)_            | File path; appends one JSON line per injection, plus one per layer-2 install.                                  |

Set `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_API` if your gateway speaks a different api (for example
`anthropic-messages` or `openai-responses`). Unlike the event hook, layer 2 sees only
the api ids it is told about.

### `raw` vs `canonical`

- `raw` sends Pi's own session id (`01a144cf-8eeb-72cd-aec1-3ee2789673ef`). Correct
  when the gateway forwards the header unchanged to the upstream OpenCode
  deployment.
- `canonical` derives `ses_…` in the same descending-timestamp + base62 layout
  OpenCode uses, so a gateway that validates the **shape** of the header also
  accepts it. The derivation is deterministic — a stable Pi session always produces
  the same id — and idempotent, so an already-canonical value passes through.

Pick `canonical` if upstream rejects a raw id for being malformed; pick `raw` if
upstream only requires a stable opaque key.

## Verify

```sh
PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_DEBUG=/tmp/oc-headers.log pi -e npm:@iam2r/pi-upstream-compat
```

Each injected request appends a line naming the layer (`event` or `api`), the model,
whether the thinking-mode compat applies to it, and the header values actually sent. A
`registry` line appears when a session start or model switch marks models, with the
`models` count. Other lines report the layer-2 install: `api-installed` (fresh wrapper,
or a new base after the host replaced ours), `api-reinstalled` (re-asserted unchanged on
`session_start`), `api-missing`, `api-incomplete`, `api-failed`.

A request is only ever modified when an injection line appears for it. Thinking-mode
compat has no line of its own: check the `thinking` field of a request's line, then the
`compat` flag on that model.

# @iam2r/pi-upstream-compat

## 0.6.2

### Patch Changes

- 35dc2b8: Make the thinking-mode compat actually apply to `models.json` providers.

  Pi's provider composer fills `reasoning: false` for every model declared in
  `models.json` without an explicit value (`provider-composer.js`:
  `definition.reasoning ?? false`), so the previous "an explicit `reasoning: false` wins"
  rule matched the _normal_ state of exactly the gateway models this extension exists for:
  nothing was ever marked, and `reasoning_content` was never replayed.

  - matching now applies regardless of the defaulted `reasoning: false`; opt out with the
    new `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_EXCLUDE` (id fragments) or `..._NO_THINKING=1`
  - models that Pi's own catalog defines are left alone (`getBuiltinModel`), so a
    non-thinking `deepseek-chat` is not redesigned as a reasoning model
  - decoration also runs at `before_agent_start`, where the catalog and the session model
    are guaranteed to be ready
  - the debug log's `registry` line reports the provider and the number of models marked

## 0.6.1

### Patch Changes

- 534bf94: Scope registry decoration to the provider a session is actually using.

  0.6.0 marked every matching model in the registry, and the registry also holds each
  built-in provider's whole catalog: on a fresh install that meant hundreds of models
  (OpenRouter's `deepseek/*`, `minimax/*`, …) were redesignated as reasoning models purely
  because of their id. Decoration now takes the session's provider
  (`ctx.model?.provider`) at `session_start`, on `model_select`, and on the header event,
  so gateway models get the flag and built-in catalogs stay exactly as Pi shipped them.

## 0.6.0

### Minor Changes

- 59ad8f1: Mark thinking-mode models in the session's model registry, so the UI agrees with the
  request builder.

  Until now the compat was only applied to the model object on its way into the request,
  which is enough for `reasoning_content` but leaves the catalog and the thinking-level
  controls reporting `thinking: no`. Pi reads capabilities from the registry
  (`AgentSession.supportsThinking()` checks `model.reasoning`), so the models are now
  decorated at `session_start`, on `model_select`, and on the main-agent header event.

  - `decorateRegistryModels()` marks every matching model in place and counts the ones
    that changed; a registry that throws is ignored rather than breaking the session.
  - Repeated session starts and model switches are idempotent.
  - An explicit `reasoning: false` still wins, and frozen models are copied.
  - The debug log gains a `registry` line with the number of models marked.

  `pi --list-models` still prints `thinking: no`: it lists the catalog without a session,
  and Pi exposes no model-registry handle at extension-load time.

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- f721d33: Rename the package from `@iam2r/pi-opencode-session-header`, and take on the
  thinking-mode replay fix it was already adjacent to.

  The package is no longer only about session headers, so the name now says what it
  does: upstream compatibility shims decided by model id.

  - New: models whose id contains a thinking family fragment (`deepseek`, `kimi`,
    `glm`, `minimax`, `mimo`) are marked `reasoning: true` with
    `compat.requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages`, so Pi replays
    `reasoning_content` on assistant turns. DeepSeek-family gateways answer
    ``400 The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API``
    without it, and Pi's own detection is URL-based, never id-based.
    - `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_THINKING_MATCH` appends extra fragments.
    - `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_NO_THINKING=1` leaves model metadata untouched.
    - an explicit `reasoning: false` in `models.json` wins, and frozen models are
      copied rather than mutated.
  - Environment variables are renamed `PI_OPENCODE_*` → `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_*`; the old
    names are still read as fallbacks. `PI_UPSTREAM_COMPAT_DEBUG` replaces
    `PI_OPENCODE_HDR_DEBUG`.
  - Debug lines now carry a `thinking` field, so an injected request says whether the
    compat applies to its model.

## 0.3.3

### Patch Changes

- 9f5ec1a: Correct the documented reason layer 2 is re-asserted, and record what was measured.

  0.3.1's changelog said Pi's bootstrap replaces the api-registry entry written while
  extensions load. That came from a probe that slept inside a `session_start` handler:
  Pi awaits handlers in load order, so the sleep delayed this extension's own handler and
  left the session id unknown — the header was missing for that reason, and the registry
  entry was in fact still ours. The real reason to re-assert is `AgentSession.reload()`,
  which serves `/reload` and session replacement and calls `resetApiProviders()`, dropping
  every api override.

  The README now also states the boundary rather than implying full coverage: a side
  request that arrives before any handler of this extension has run cannot carry a session
  id, because the request has no session information of its own and `ExtensionAPI` exposes
  no session getter outside an event context. Requests after the first handler are
  covered, including the `ctx.modelRegistry.streamSimple(...)` path layer 2 exists for.

## 0.3.2

### Patch Changes

- cd3fc7c: Resolve the layer-2 session id on demand, and correct the README.

  The wrapper now reads the id instead of only trusting a snapshot: the cached value,
  then the live session, then the session file name (`<timestamp>_<id>.jsonl`). A
  context captured before a reload counts as no answer instead of throwing. Extracted
  to `session-source.ts` with unit tests.

  This is hardening, not a fix for a reproduced failure: at this extension's
  `session_start` the id is already there (measured), so the cache is normally
  populated first. It matters when that is not the case, since Pi awaits event handlers
  in load order and one slow handler delays every handler after it.

  The README no longer claims the wrapper is wiped by Pi's bootstrap; it names the
  `resetApiProviders()` reload path, and records the boundary that a side request
  arriving before any handler of this extension has run cannot carry a session id.

## 0.3.1

### Patch Changes

- a8b3aa1: Re-assert the api-layer wrapper on every `session_start`.

  `AgentSession.reload()` (`core/agent-session.js`), which serves `/reload` and session
  replacement, calls `resetApiProviders()`: every api registration is dropped and only
  the built-ins are put back. The wrapper is now installed while the factory runs _and_
  re-asserted on each `session_start`, so it is present again after such a reload.

  Re-installing is idempotent. The host registry keeps one entry per api and does not
  say who owns it, so `unregisterApiProviders(<our source>)` doubles as the probe:
  removing our own entry empties the slot while we still own it, and leaves the host's
  implementation visible when we no longer do — that implementation is then adopted as
  the new base. Wrappers always delegate to a captured base, never to the registry, so
  repeated installs cannot stack.

  `PI_OPENCODE_HDR_DEBUG` now distinguishes `api-installed` (fresh wrapper, or a new
  base) from `api-reinstalled` (re-asserted unchanged).

  Correction: this entry originally described the wrapper as wiped by Pi's bootstrap
  after extension loading. That came from a probe that slept inside a `session_start`
  handler, which delayed this extension's own handler and left the session id unknown,
  so the header was missing for a different reason. The registry entry was in fact
  still ours; the reload path above is the real reason to re-assert.

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- d81f756: Layer 2 now actually runs: it wraps the api implementation at extension-load time
  instead of registering a provider from a `session_start` handler.

  The provider registration was silently dropped. After extension loading,
  `pi.registerProvider(...)` only appends to `runtime.pendingProviderRegistrations`,
  and the host drains that queue once, while extensions load — so the call returned
  normally and layer 2 was never installed. Requests that bypass the
  `before_provider_headers` event (any `ctx.modelRegistry.streamSimple(...)` caller,
  such as pi-subagents' pruned-fork summaries) went out with no session header at all.

  Layer 2 is now `registerApiProvider()` around the `PI_OPENCODE_API` implementation,
  installed while the factory runs. It covers every caller and every provider serving
  that api — no provider id needed.

  Because of that:

  - `PI_OPENCODE_PROVIDER` is gone; layer 2 no longer targets a provider by name.
  - `PI_OPENCODE_API` is now a comma-separated list of api ids to wrap.
  - `PI_OPENCODE_NO_PROVIDER=1` still disables layer 2.
  - `PI_OPENCODE_HDR_DEBUG` logs `api-installed`/`api-missing` and reports injections
    from layer 2 with `layer: "api"` (`event` for layer 1, as before).

  Verified with a gateway configured as a plain `openai-completions` provider: the
  main agent loop injects via the event layer, and a direct `streamSimple` call with
  no prior event injects via the api layer.

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

- 04a9b48: Spell out in the README that `PI_OPENCODE_PROVIDER` defaults to `Agate`.

  On any other machine it has to be set to your own provider id, or layer 2 is
  never registered and only the event hook applies — enough for the main agent,
  but not for direct `streamSimple` side requests.

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 1d0082f: Add `PI_OPENCODE_MODEL_MATCH`, for gateways that rename their OpenCode models.

  Matching keyed off the model id containing `opencode`, so a gateway that serves an
  upstream OpenCode model under a name of its own — `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, say —
  received no session header at all, and failed silently. `PI_OPENCODE_MODEL_MATCH`
  takes a comma-separated list of extra substrings to treat as OpenCode too; the
  built-in `opencode` match is kept and matching stays case-insensitive.

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- Initial release. Attaches OpenCode's session-affinity headers
  (`x-opencode-session`, plus `x-opencode-client: pi`) to any model whose id
  mentions `opencode`, including models served through third-party gateways
  that Pi would not otherwise treat as OpenCode.

  Two layers cooperate: a `before_provider_headers` hook covers the main agent,
  and a registered `streamSimple` wrapper covers every other caller such as
  subagent pruned forks. A header that is already present is never overwritten.
